newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM may win parliament vote to form govt.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM may win parliament vote to form govt.

text.p: Slovenia's acting centre-left prime minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday appeared likely to win a parliamentary vote to form the next government after a rightwing deputy defected from his party.

Ciril Pucko, a member of the Christian Democrats -- one of three parties belonging to a rightwing alliance hoping to defeat Drnovsek -- had quit the party, a senior member of Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats told Reuters.

"Pucko has decided to support Drnovsek's candidacy (for prime minister). He has left the Christian Democrats and will take his seat as an independent deputy," the leader of the Liberal Democrats parliamentary group Tone Anderlic said.
Parliamentary speaker Janez Podobnik confirmed that Pucko had defected and said he had postponed the parliamentary vote, which had been due at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT), until 12.30 p.m. (1130 GMT).
"I was just informed that Ciril Pucko decided to leave the parliamentary group of the Christian Democrats today," Podobnik said.
Three rightwing parties of the so-called "Spring" alliance were counting on Drnovsek losing the parliamentary vote to give them the chance to form the next government.
